    The k-linear category of a basic algebra #

    Section 3.3 of the manuscript fixes a complete set of primitive orthogonal idempotents e_i of the basic algebra A and considers the k-linear category 𝒜 with these vertices as objects and morphism spaces 𝒜(i, j) = e_j A e_i, composition being multiplication. It identifies A-modules with 𝒜-modules.

    This file defines

    • LinMod k C: modules over a k-linear category C, that is, k-linear functors C ⥤ Mod k;
    • IdempotentFamily A ι: a complete family e : ι → A of orthogonal idempotents (primitivity is never used, so it is not recorded);
    • AlgebraCategory k E: the category 𝒜;
    • AlgebraCategory.toModule: the functor M ↦ ⊕ᵢ M(i) from 𝒜-modules to A-modules, where a acts through the blocks e_j a e_i. It is k-linear, fully faithful (fullyFaithfulToModule), exact and faithful (range_map_eq_ker_map, injective_map_iff, surjective_map_iff), and it preserves finite dimension (finite_toModule); its underlying k-space is ∏ᵢ M(i) (restrictScalarsEquiv).

          Complete families of orthogonal idempotents #

          source
          structure LargeIndecomposable.IdempotentFamily (A : Type u) [Ring A] (ι : Type u) [Fintype ι] :
          Type u

          A complete family of orthogonal idempotents e : ι → A: idempotent, pairwise orthogonal, with sum 1. In the manuscript the e_i are moreover primitive (the vertices of the basic algebra A); primitivity is not used in the constructions of this file.

          • e : ι → A

            The idempotents.

          • mul_self (i : ι) : self.e i * self.e i = self.e i
          • mul_eq_zero (i j : ι) : i ≠ j → self.e i * self.e j = 0
          • sum_eq_one : ∑ i : ι, self.e i = 1
